info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Generated from the live router — every operation below is a route the unified cloud binary actually serves. Tagged by product: the first path segment after /v1/.

get.summary: ListAgents returns every agent defined in the caller's org, each with the number of runs recorded against it.
get.description:
ListAgents returns every agent defined in the caller's org, each with the
number of runs recorded against it.

post.summary: CreateAgent defines an agent in the caller's org: a model, a system prompt (instructions) and a set of tool names.
post.description:
CreateAgent defines an agent in the caller's org: a model, a system prompt
(instructions) and a set of tool names. The name must be unique in the org and
match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$. An omitted model takes the
deployment's configured default; a named one is checked against the gateway's
served catalog, so a model this deployment never serves is refused here rather
than failing at run time. A long-running agent must carry a 5-field cron
schedule (the scheduler would otherwise never fire it) and counts against a
per-org cap on scheduled agents.

get.summary: AgentActivity serves the org-wide recent-activity feed.
get.description:
AgentActivity serves the org-wide recent-activity feed. Events are REAL: each
recorded run is an invoked (ok) or failed (error) event; each agent's own
create/update timestamps are created/updated events. Merged, newest first,
capped. Nothing is invented — an org with no agents and no runs gets [].

get.summary: ListBuilds returns the public index of every published build, most recently updated first, so a gallery can link straight to the story behind each product.
get.description:
ListBuilds returns the public index of every published build, most recently
updated first, so a gallery can link straight to the story behind each product.
PUBLIC, no tenancy: publishing is the author's act, and only published root
sessions appear here.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the page. Absent, zero or over 500 reads as 100.

get.summary: ReadBuild returns the readable build of one product: the agent session that produced it, turn by turn — the prompts, the reasoning, the commits each turn produced — plus the exact `git log` that re-derives every commit binding from git itself, so nothing here has to be taken on trust.
get.description:
ReadBuild returns the readable build of one product: the agent session that
produced it, turn by turn — the prompts, the reasoning, the commits each turn
produced — plus the exact `git log` that re-derives every commit binding from
git itself, so nothing here has to be taken on trust.

PUBLIC, no tenancy: it answers only for a session its author explicitly
published, which is what makes it safe to be anonymous. An unpublished session
is invisible here no matter who asks; its owner reads it through the org-scoped
/v1/agents/sessions routes, which need a validated principal.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org is the org that published the build, from the path.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project is the product's slug, from the path.

get.summary: AgentMetrics serves the invocations-over-time histogram for the org's Agents dashboard.
get.description:
AgentMetrics serves the invocations-over-time histogram for the org's Agents
dashboard. Every point is a REAL count of recorded runs in that time bucket —
one series line per agent that ran in the window. The Resource Usage rollup is
all-null because this store meters no CPU/memory/storage/cost; the console
renders those as "—" rather than a fabricated figure. No runs => empty series
(an honest "not connected / no activity yet"), never a synthesized trend.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: Range is the window to bucket: 24H, 7D or 30D. Anything else reads as 30D.

get.summary: ListSessions returns the caller org's live sessions, newest first — each with its event count, its direct-child count and a one-line preview of its latest event.
get.description:
ListSessions returns the caller org's live sessions, newest first — each with
its event count, its direct-child count and a one-line preview of its latest
event. With no filter it returns ROOT sessions only, so a dashboard shows one
row per flow rather than one per subagent; ?root= or ?parent= descends.

parameters.name: root
parameters.description: Root scopes the page to one subagent tree (its root session id).

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description:
Parent scopes the page to the direct children of one session. Ignored when
root is set; with neither, only ROOT sessions come back.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Status filters to running, paused, done or error.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project filters to the sessions tagged with one product slug.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the page. Absent, zero or over 500 reads as 100.

post.summary: RegisterSession opens a live agent session in the caller's org — the row every surface (the CLI's outer agent, hanzo.bot, the console, chat) hangs its activity off.
post.description:
RegisterSession opens a live agent session in the caller's org — the row every
surface (the CLI's outer agent, hanzo.bot, the console, chat) hangs its
activity off. A session with a parentSessionId becomes a subagent of that
session and inherits its root, so one flow is one tree; without one it is
itself a root. Registering with a terminal status records a session that has
already finished.

get.summary: GetSession returns one session with its direct child sessions and its 50 most recent events, oldest of those first.
get.description:
GetSession returns one session with its direct child sessions and its 50 most
recent events, oldest of those first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to act on, from the path.

patch.summary: PatchSession updates a session's surface-owned truth: its status, its title, the run-target it is dispatched to, and the product it built plus whether that build's story is public.
patch.description:
PatchSession updates a session's surface-owned truth: its status, its title,
the run-target it is dispatched to, and the product it built plus whether that
build's story is public. A FINISHED session stays finished — reopening a
done/error run would fabricate liveness — and publishing is refused unless the
session names the project it built, because the public build route is keyed on
(org, project).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to update, from the path.

get.summary: DrainSessionControl returns the steering commands (pause/resume/stop/message) recorded against the caller's own session that are newer than the cursor, oldest first, with the cursor to poll from next.
get.description:
DrainSessionControl returns the steering commands (pause/resume/stop/message)
recorded against the caller's own session that are newer than the cursor,
oldest first, with the cursor to poll from next. It is how a locally started
`hanzo code` session — which is not task-backed, so nothing forwards its
commands to an execution engine — consumes what the dashboard posted. Read-only
and bounded at 200 per poll, so a steady poll is cheap and an applied command is
never redelivered.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session whose commands are being drained, from the path.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
After is the last seq this poller applied; only commands newer than it come
back. Absent or negative reads as 0, which drains from the beginning.

get.summary: SessionTree returns the subagent-flow graph rooted at this session: the session, its children, their children, each node carrying its own event count.
get.description:
SessionTree returns the subagent-flow graph rooted at this session: the session,
its children, their children, each node carrying its own event count. One
indexed read pulls the whole flow (every node of a flow shares a root id), so
the shape is assembled in memory rather than by walking the store per node.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to act on, from the path.

get.summary: ListTargets returns every machine registered to the caller's org, newest first, each with its live session load.
get.description:
ListTargets returns every machine registered to the caller's org, newest
first, each with its live session load.

post.summary: RegisterTarget registers a machine as an agent target, or re-links one that is already registered.
post.description:
RegisterTarget registers a machine as an agent target, or re-links one that is
already registered. Re-linking is idempotent and keyed on org+host+owner, so a
machine that reconnects refreshes its own row rather than piling up duplicates;
it answers 200, while a first registration answers 201.

delete.description:
DeleteTarget deregisters one machine. Only its owner, or an org admin, may
remove it; an unknown id, a cross-org id and a machine owned by someone else
all answer the same not-found, so a probe learns nothing about what exists.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the target to act on, from the path.

get.summary: GetTarget returns one registered machine, with its live session load.
get.description: GetTarget returns one registered machine, with its live session load.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the target to act on, from the path.

patch.summary: PatchTarget updates one machine in place.
patch.description:
PatchTarget updates one machine in place. Every field is optional; a field the
request omits is left alone. A metrics patch IS a heartbeat — the server stamps
its own clock, so a client can neither forge nor backdate staleness.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the target to update, from the path.

post.summary: ClaimRoutedRun is the machine's long poll for work: it authenticates the daemon, stamps the liveness the dispatch gate reads (the poll IS the proof a runner is listening), and waits up to 25 seconds for the next run addressed to THIS machine.
post.description:
ClaimRoutedRun is the machine's long poll for work: it authenticates the
daemon, stamps the liveness the dispatch gate reads (the poll IS the proof a
runner is listening), and waits up to 25 seconds for the next run addressed to
THIS machine. It answers the run when one arrives and 204 with no body when the
window elapses, on which the daemon re-polls immediately.

TWO independent proofs are required and both fail closed to the same 403: the
caller must own this machine (or be an org admin) AND present its claim key in
X-Target-Key. A run offered to one machine is unreachable from another's claim.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the target to act on, from the path.

post.summary: MintTargetClaimKey mints (or rotates) the claim key a `hanzo code --serve` daemon presents to claim work for this machine, and returns it ONCE: only its SHA-256 hash is stored.
post.description:
MintTargetClaimKey mints (or rotates) the claim key a `hanzo code --serve`
daemon presents to claim work for this machine, and returns it ONCE: only its
SHA-256 hash is stored. Rotating supersedes any prior daemon, so only the
machine's owner — or an org admin — may call it; every other caller gets the
same not-found an unknown id gets, and learns nothing about what exists.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the target to act on, from the path.

post.summary: ReportRoutedRun completes a claimed run: it delivers the terminal result to the run's durable owner, which is what lets that workflow finish.
post.description:
ReportRoutedRun completes a claimed run: it delivers the terminal result to the
run's durable owner, which is what lets that workflow finish. Scoped to (org,
target, run) and claim-key-authenticated, so a machine can only ever report a
run it legitimately holds. Idempotent — a report for an unknown or
already-finished run answers delivered:false rather than failing, because the
session's terminal state was already set by the machine's own stream.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the machine reporting, from the path.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: RunID is the routed run being completed, from the path.

delete.summary: DeleteAgent removes an agent and every run recorded against it.
delete.description: DeleteAgent removes an agent and every run recorded against it. Answers 204.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description:
Ref is the agent's public id (the agent_… handle create and list return) or
its org-unique name, from the path. Either resolves the same agent.

get.summary: GetAgent returns one agent with its system prompt and its 20 most recent runs.
get.description:
GetAgent returns one agent with its system prompt and its 20 most recent runs.
The ref is the agent's public id or its org-unique name — a created agent is
immediately gettable by whatever create handed back.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description:
Ref is the agent's public id (the agent_… handle create and list return) or
its org-unique name, from the path. Either resolves the same agent.

patch.summary: UpdateAgent changes an agent in place.
patch.description:
UpdateAgent changes an agent in place. Every field is optional; a field the
request omits keeps its stored value. The resulting mode+schedule are
re-validated together, so a partial update can never leave a long-running
agent without the cron the scheduler needs to fire it, and a transition INTO
long-running counts against the per-org cap on scheduled agents.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is the agent to update — its public id or org-unique name, from the path.

get.summary: ListAgentRuns returns one agent's execution history, newest first — each run's input, its output or its error, and how long it took.
get.description:
ListAgentRuns returns one agent's execution history, newest first — each run's
input, its output or its error, and how long it took. Every row is a run that
actually happened.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is the agent's public id or its org-unique name, from the path.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit caps how many runs come back, newest first. Absent, zero or out of
range (1..200) reads as 50.

activity.description: Activity is the merged run/create/update events, newest first, capped at 50.

agents.description: Agents is the org's agents, each carrying its recorded run count.

builds.description: Builds is every published build, most recently updated first.

verify.description:
Verify is the exact command that re-derives every commit binding below
straight from git, so nothing here has to be taken on trust.

claimKey.description:
ClaimKey is the capability itself. It is returned ONCE and never again — only
its SHA-256 hash is stored — so a daemon that loses it mints a new one.

targetId.description: TargetID is the machine the key authenticates.

commands.description: Commands is the session's control commands newer than the cursor, oldest first.

cursor.description:
Cursor is the seq to send as `after` on the next poll — the highest seq in
this page, or the cursor sent in when the page is empty.

id.description: ID is the session to update, from the path.

project.description:
Project tags the product this session built; Published is the author's
decision to let anyone read the story (provenance.go). Both are pointers so
"absent" and "cleared" are different requests.

target.description: Target re-dispatches a session to a run-target (the #48 association). "" detaches.

id.description: ID is the target to update, from the path.

metrics.description: present => a heartbeat; the server stamps its time

host.description: Execution context — where this session runs (all optional).

project.description:
The readable build (provenance.go): which product this session builds, and
whether its story may be read by the world.

provider.description: Account tag — the linked AI account this session ran under (login manager).

delivered.description:
Delivered is true when a waiting durable owner received this result. False
means there was none to deliver to — an unknown or already-finished run — which
is a clean no-op, not an error.

branch.description:
Branch, CommitSha and Diffstat describe what the run produced; Error is the
failure when OK is false. Each is clamped, never rejected.

id.description: ID is the machine reporting, from the path.

ok.description: OK is whether the run succeeded; Changed whether it produced any commit.

runId.description: RunID is the routed run being completed, from the path.

repo.description: Repo is the repository to work in and CloneURL is how to fetch it.

sessionId.description:
SessionID is the live session opened at dispatch; the machine streams its
turns into it.

timeoutSeconds.description: TimeoutSeconds bounds the run on the machine; 0 means the machine's own default.

runs.description: Runs is the agent's executions, newest first.

v.description: real invocation count in the bucket

sessions.description:
Sessions is the matching sessions, each with its event and child counts and
a one-line preview of its latest event.

host.description:
Execution context (mission-control): the machine/repo/cwd a card shows and
the run-target a session is dispatched to. Omitted when a surface didn't report it.

lastEvent.description:
LastEvent is the compact latest-activity line for the list projection (nil in
register/patch/tree responses; set by list + detail). It lets a swipe card show
a live one-line preview without fetching full detail.

org.description:
Org is the caller's OWN tenant, echoed so a client can build the public
build URL (/builds/:org/:project) without a second call or a guess. It is
never another tenant's — every read is org-scoped before it gets here.

project.description:
The readable build: the product this session built and whether its story
is public (provenance.go).

deleted.description: Deleted is true when the target was removed.

id.description: ID is the target that was removed.

targets.description: Targets is every target registered to the caller's org.

ref.description: Ref is the agent to update — its public id or org-unique name, from the path.
